newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian election challenger attacked at rally.
newsitem.headline: Croatian election challenger attacked at rally.

text.p: Vlado Gotovac, one of two challengers to Croatian President Franjo Tudjman in next week's presidential election, was struck on the head at a rally and has been flown to hospital, a party spokesman said on Friday.
Gotovac is suffering from concussion and is in shock and was flown to a Zagreb hospital by helicopter for medical checks, the spokesman told Reuters.

Gotovac was struck by a man wearing army uniform at a rally in the town of Pula on the Istrian peninsula late on Thursday. He then fell and hit his head on a loudspeaker but recovered enough to go on to make a speech.
Reports said the attacker was immediately arrested.

The 66-year-old leader of the Social Liberal party is fighting an uphill battle to try and oust Tudjman who is expected to win the election on June 15 outright, with between 60 and 70 percent of the votes in the first round.

Gotovac and the other opposition candidate, Zdravko Tomac of the Social Democratic party, are touring the country in a frenetic dash to convince voters it is time to change the country's autocratic form of government.
Tomac is driving around in a small blue van which was stoned by protesters on the first day of the campaign last week.
